data-act: When does the Data Act apply?

Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 has applied since 12 September 2025, with staggered deadlines: data access by design covers connected products placed on the market from 12-9-2026, and charges for switching cloud provider disappear on 12-1-2027.
What does the Data Act change for cloud providers?

They must make it easy for customers to switch provider or move to their own infrastructure: maximum notice periods, data export and assistance during the migration. From 12-1-2027 switching can carry no exit charges.
Each Member State designates its authorities (Art. 37) and sets the penalties (Art. 40). Where personal data are involved, GDPR fines also apply.
cra: Which products does the CRA cover?
Every product with digital elements placed on the EU market, hardware or software, throughout its life cycle. Cybersecurity becomes a requirement for CE marking.
When must companies comply with the CRA?

Reporting actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents has been mandatory since 11-9-2026, through ENISA's single reporting platform. The other obligations, including CE marking, apply from 11-12-2027.
What fines does the CRA set?

Up to €15 million or 2.5% of worldwide turnover for breaching the essential requirements; up to €10 million or 2% for other obligations; and up to €5 million or 1% for supplying incorrect information.
nis2: Which companies does NIS2 apply to?

Essential and important entities in critical sectors, depending on their size; in the digital sector this includes cloud providers, data centres and managed service providers. Other suppliers are affected indirectly through contracts with customers that are in scope.
How quickly must an incident be reported under NIS2?
An early warning within 24 hours, an incident notification within 72 hours and a final report within one month, sent to the national CSIRT or competent authority.
What penalties does NIS2 provide for?
Up to €10 million or 2% of worldwide turnover for essential entities and up to €7 million or 1.4% for important entities. Each Member State sets them out in its transposition law.
csa2-eucs: The Commission's proposal COM(2026) 11 of 20-1-2026 to replace the 2019 Cybersecurity Act: it strengthens ENISA, speeds up European certification and allows high-risk suppliers from third countries to be designated.
Is the CSA2 already in force?
No. It is a proposal at first reading in Parliament; the Council presented a progress report on 22-5-2026. The Cybersecurity Act and its schemes, such as EUCC, remain in force.
What happens to high-risk suppliers under the CSA2?

The proposal would allow them to be identified and their components to be removed from critical infrastructure, with fines of up to 7% of worldwide turnover. It is worth mapping suppliers and components by country of control now.
dora: To 21 types of EU financial entity and, through their contracts, to the ICT providers that serve them. It has applied since 17 January 2025.
What must contracts with ICT providers include?
Article 30 sets minimum clauses: description of services, data locations, service levels, cooperation with authorities, audit rights and exit strategies.

The European Supervisory Authorities EBA, EIOPA and ESMA. On 18-11-2025 they designated 19 critical ICT third-party providers, which can face periodic penalty payments of up to 1% of their average daily worldwide turnover.
dma-nube: Have AWS and Azure been designated under the DMA?
On 25-6-2026 the Commission preliminarily concluded that they should be gatekeepers for their cloud services. Formal designation has not yet taken place.
What would AWS and Azure have to comply with?
Interoperability, data portability and non-self-preferencing obligations, including for their AI tools, within six months of designation.
What fines does the DMA provide for?
Only the European Commission enforces it. Fines reach 10% of worldwide turnover and 20% for repeat infringements.
ehds: Regulation (EU) 2025/327 entered into force on 26-3-2025; general application starts on 26-3-2027 and continues in phases until 2035.
What changes for electronic health record manufacturers?
Their systems must be interoperable with the European format and carry CE marking; for the first group of data categories, from 26-3-2029.
Can health data be reused for research and AI?
Yes, through data permits granted by national health data access bodies, and always in secure processing environments, without handing over the raw data.
rgpd-omnibus: Has the Digital Omnibus already changed the GDPR?
No. It is a Commission proposal of 19-11-2025 still under negotiation: the Council adopted its position in October 2026 and Parliament is still at committee stage. The current GDPR applies.
What does the Omnibus propose on personal data?

It would change the definition of personal data, cookies, the use of data to train AI and breach notification. Data protection authorities and several Member States have slowed down the deepest changes.
What is the new GDPR procedural regulation?
Regulation (EU) 2025/2518 harmonises procedures in cross-border cases and applies from 2-4-2027.
data-union: What is the Data Union Strategy?
A Commission communication, COM(2025) 835 of 19-11-2025, aiming at more high-quality data for AI, simpler rules and a firm policy on international data flows.
Is the Data Union Strategy binding?
It has no direct legal effect: it is implemented through other laws and programmes, such as the Digital Omnibus, the common European data spaces and the Cloud and AI Development Act.
What funding does the Data Union Strategy announce?
An additional €100 million for common European data spaces from 2026, plus data labs and AI Factories.
chips-act: Proposal COM(2026) 504 of 3-6-2026, which would repeal the 2023 European Chips Act and shift the focus to demand: innovative public procurement, demand accelerators and chips for AI.
No. It is a proposed regulation presented with the CADA in the tech sovereignty package and is being negotiated by Parliament and the Council.
What is the EU's target for chips?
20% of world production by 2030, although forecasts point to a real share of around 11.7%.
ecodiseno-servidores: What does the ecodesign regulation require of servers?
Power supply efficiency, idle power limits, secure data deletion, firmware updates and information on materials. It has applied since 1-3-2020 to servers and online data storage products.
Who must comply with the server ecodesign regulation?
The manufacturer, importer or authorised representative placing the product on the EU market, with CE marking and technical documentation.
What efficiency obligations do data centres have?
Those of 500 kW or more report their energy performance every year to the European database; the next report is due on 15-5-2027, and the Commission is preparing an A–G efficiency label.
raee: Who is a WEEE producer in Spain?
Anyone placing electrical or electronic equipment on the Spanish market: manufacturer, importer or distance seller. They must register, report what they sell and finance collection and treatment.
Are servers and network equipment covered by WEEE rules?
Yes. Since 15-8-2018 the scope is open: all electrical and electronic equipment unless expressly excluded.
Which law governs WEEE in Spain?
Royal Decree 110/2015, amended by Royal Decree 27/2021, which transposes Directive 2012/19/EU within the framework of Law 7/2022 on waste.
factura-electronica: When will B2B e-invoicing become mandatory in Spain?
From 6 October 2027 for companies with turnover above €8 million and from 6 October 2028 for all others, under Royal Decree 238/2026.
Is e-invoicing the same as VERI*FACTU?
No. VERI*FACTU regulates invoicing software (Royal Decree 1007/2023) and is expected to be postponed to October 2028; B2B e-invoicing is a separate obligation.
What about e-invoicing at EU level?
Directive (EU) 2025/516 (ViDA) will make e-invoicing mandatory for intra-EU transactions from 1-7-2030.
ens: Who must comply with Spain's ENS?
The whole Spanish public sector and the suppliers providing it with technology services or solutions, under Royal Decree 311/2022.
Each system is categorised (basic, medium or high), a risk analysis and statement of applicability of the 73 measures are prepared, and an audit is passed, renewed every two years.
Does the ENS help with NIS2 or EUCS?
Until the European EUCS scheme and Spain's NIS2 law exist, it is the most solid national reference, and many of its measures cover what those laws require.
ley-gobernanza-ia: Is Spain's AI governance law in force?
No. The organic law bill reached Congress in June 2026 but lapsed when Parliament was dissolved on 6 October 2026.
Does that mean the AI Act does not apply in Spain?
It does apply: it is a directly applicable EU regulation. What is missing is the national law on authorities, penalties and the use of AI in the public sector.
What should companies do until Spain has an AI law?
Inventory their AI systems, classify them by risk, train staff, use AESIA's guidance and follow the AI Omnibus deadlines for high-risk systems: December 2027 and August 2028.
rd-centros-datos: Has Spain's data centre decree been approved?
Not yet. It is a draft processed under the urgent procedure, with a public hearing from 27-8 to 10-9-2026; approval by the Council of Ministers is expected in November 2026.
Which data centres would the decree apply to?
Under the October text, those with an access capacity of 10 MW or more; the digital sovereignty requirements apply regardless of capacity.
What happens if a data centre does not meet the requirements?
Grid access and connection permits are not granted, or those already granted are lost.
ai-act: When does the AI Act apply?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 applies in stages: prohibited practices since 2-2-2025, general-purpose AI model obligations since 2-8-2025, and most other rules from 2-8-2026. The AI Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, moved the high-risk deadlines to December 2027 and August 2028.
Who must comply with the AI Act?

Providers that place AI systems on the EU market, deployers that use them in a professional capacity, and importers and distributors, including companies outside the EU whose systems are used in the Union.
What fines does the AI Act set?
Up to €35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover for prohibited practices, up to €15 million or 3% for most other obligations, and up to €7.5 million or 1% for supplying incorrect information.
